rationale: The source moves from true opinions in the boy, through repeated questioning and stabilization, to claims about prior possession, prior time, immortality, recollection, and willingness to defend inquiry. Preserve these steps separately, including Socrates' explicit refusal at 86b to insist on every other detail of the account. At 85b-86b the record combines the boy's ownership of his answers, latent true opinions, their conversion to knowledge through repeated questioning, prenatal acquisition, immortality, and recollection. These are successive inferences, not one textual fact; split them and preserve explicit dependencies. Recorded once at the observation start.
